Trucking responsible for nearly $110 billion in cross-border freight for September
item.description: Freight trucks moved $109.7 billion in goods across the U.S. border with Canada and Mexico in September 2026, a 27.6% gain on the prior year, according to Bureau of Transportation Statistics data released Nov. 13. All modes combined handled $161.1 billion, up 23.4%, and trucks made up 68% of that, more than six times rail's share. Mexico accounted for nearly 69% of truck value, at $75.4 billion, versus $34.3 billion for Canada. The data include imports and exports and are in current dollars, not adjusted for inflation, and they do not count truckloads or trucks crossing. The agency named Laredo and El Paso, Texas, and Otay Mesa, California, as leading truck crossings for Mexico freight, and Detroit and Port Huron, Michigan, and Buffalo, New York, for Canada.

item.title: DAT: Van spot rates hit $3.11 as truck availability climbs 9%
item.description: DAT Freight & Analytics reported that broker-to-carrier spot rates for van averaged $3.11 a mile for the week of Nov. 7-13, up 4 cents, with reefer at $3.70 and flatbed at $3.61. Total equipment posts rose 9% to 187,501, while load posts fell 6% from the prior week to 2.70 million. Dean Croke, an industry analyst at DAT, said van linehaul rates are 36% above last year. Croke said year-over-year gains should narrow after Thanksgiving, which falls on Nov. 26, as van and reefer rates typically build into the holiday weeks. DAT's 35-day forecast has van linehaul rising to $2.36 a mile by Dec. 17.

USPS is set to make fuel surcharge permanent, raise parcel prices 5.9% in 2027
item.description: USPS wants its fuel surcharge made permanent, with the rate climbing from 8% to 11% on Jan. 17. The Postal Service has also proposed an average rate increase of 5.9% for four domestic package services, including Ground Advantage and Priority Mail. The changes were filed with the Postal Regulatory Commission on Thursday, after the Board of Governors approved them. The surcharge began in April as a temporary 8% increase set to expire Jan. 17, and USPS cited rising fuel prices in proposing the three-point hike. International products are not covered by the surcharge for now, but several international services would rise an average of 7.9%, and USPS is reworking its country rate groups.

Congressman Taylor Champions Legislation to Codify CDL Fraud Tipline
item.description: Representative Dave Taylor (OH-02) introduced H.R. 11031, the CDL Fraud Tipline Act, which would make the Department of Homeland Security's CDL fraud tipline permanent in law. According to the release, the public can report suspected CDL fraud by calling (866) 347-2423, and the aim is to keep unqualified drivers from causing crashes. Ten other House members signed on as cosponsors. American Truckers United, which is a supporting organization of the bill, said fraudulent CDLs let underqualified drivers operate 80,000-pound trucks and cost truckers their livelihoods.

Bipartisan bill to require truck driver bathroom access at shippers and receivers
item.description: Two senators from opposite parties, Deb Fischer (R-Neb.) and Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.), introduced the Trucker Bathroom Access Bill on November 12, 2026, and a companion version was introduced in the House. If passed, the measure would give drivers picking up or delivering freight the same restroom access as a business’s customers or employees, at shippers, receivers, manufacturers, warehouses and distribution centers. The bill would not require businesses to build new restroom facilities. Several trucking groups have endorsed it, including the Owner-Operator Independent Drivers Association, the American Trucking Association, Women in Trucking Association, She Trucking and Trinity Logistics.

Humble Robotics founder Eyal Cohen: self-driving trucks should be built without a driver's cab, and regulation is the real brake
item.description: Humble Robotics, which builds its trucks in San Francisco, has raised a $51 million Series A that brings its total funding to $75 million, according to an interview with founder Eyal Cohen on the MTS podcast. Cohen said the money will go toward building more vehicles, testing them, and running customer pilots to begin moving freight, with pilots targeted "in the next year," roughly late 2027. He argued that regulation is a major constraint, noting that some truck rules were written about 100 years ago and that a radically redesigned vehicle must still comply with federal, state and local laws.

item.title: CHP cites truck driver after spotting 20 MPH speed violation and 'numerous' tire defects on I-5
item.description: The California Highway Patrol said an officer from its Williams Division stopped a truck on I-5 last week for exceeding the speed limit by more than 20 mph. During the stop, the officer found what the agency called numerous safety problems with the tires on the vehicle combination. The driver was cited for multiple violations and ordered out of service until the equipment was repaired. CHP said troopers will keep targeting speeding and reckless driving in Colusa County. The agency also reminded truckers that California sets a 55 mph limit for truck tractors with three or more axles.

New York Overturned a CDL Penalty. Can California Recover $31 Million Already Withheld?
item.description:
A federal appeals court in the Second Circuit on November 13 set aside a $73.5 million federal funding penalty against New York over nondomiciled commercial driver's licenses. The court found that federal officials were trying to enforce a licensing requirement that the governing regulations did not contain. Parriva asks whether California can use the same reasoning to challenge its own penalty.
An October 1 Federal Highway Administration notice shows $31,229,953 withheld from California, covering the period October 1 through December 11, 2026. California's separate dispute involves an estimated $158.3 million in fiscal 2027 highway funding, which does not mean that full amount has been withheld. The California case is docketed as No. 26-1027 before the D.C. Circuit and was scheduled for oral argument on September 11, 2026. Parriva said it could not verify a final merits decision as of November 14.
